page.overview:
Who is Pan?

Pan is an ancient Greek god often associated with pastoral scenery, music and fertility. He is typically represented as a humanoid figure with the legs and horns of a goat, similar to the mythic fauns. His name is the origin of the word panic.

In ancient times, the god Pan was said to dwell in Mount Maenalus, in Arcadia, and was accompanied by strange creatures named Panisci. (: "The Tree")

Later on, Pan and the other gods entered a death-like sleep, but shall wake up and reclaim their domains someday. (: "Poetry and the Gods")

In The Great God Pan, by Arthur Machen, the titular deity is unseen, but plays a pivotal role by impregnating a woman who took part in a scientific experiment to see beyond the fabric of reality (similar to H. P. Lovecraft's "From Beyond"). This union results in the birth of a deceptively human child named Helen Vaughan, who grows up to commit terrible acts (: The Great God Pan). In Lovecraft's "The Dunwich Horror", Henry Armitage mentions Machen's story in connection to the case of Wilbur Whateley.
